data.text:
Claim on an existing branch leaves a conflicted merge and reports success
Second instance: claiming LS-worker-lane-override (branch 12673 commits behind main) left the new worktree mid-merge with an UD path on the split ddflow/services/adopt.py; claim answered how=created with no warning. Source: infra/worktree/_create.py ignores the GitResult of sync(wt, cfg).

chunk_findings.detail: The previous LOW still holds. The `parse_lane_tiers` change now rejects case-variant duplicates in the current spec, but it does not update `write_lanes`' orphan check, which compares existing lane file names case-sensitively. On a case-insensitive, case-preserving filesystem (macOS/Windows defaults), changing `mcp.lane_tools = "IMPL=all"` to `mcp.lane_tools = "impl=all"` leaves `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-IMPL.json` not recognized as the existing file for lane `impl`, so adopt misreports or rewrites the same file instead of treating it as current.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:write_lanes

chunk_findings.detail: `_LANE_NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*")` requires the first character to be alphanumeric, but the adjacent comment says only a leading dot is forbidden and the knob doc says a lane name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`. For example, `mcp.lane_tools = "_impl=all"` or `"-impl=all"` raises `ValueError` even though both are valid according to the stated allowed characters and would produce valid file names. If leading `_` and `-` are actually meant to be invalid, the comment/doc are wrong; otherwise the regex should allow either as the first character.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/mcp.py:26

chunk_findings.detail: `wide` is sorted lexicographically by lane name (`sorted(lane for lane, tier in lanes.items() if deferral_note(env, tier=tier))`), but then the returned note uses `deferral_note(env, tier=lanes[wide[0]])`. The docstring says the note should be "for the widest" deferral, yet the widest is not the alphabetically first lane. For example, with `[mcp].lane_tools = "alpha=narrow_defer, zeta=wide_defer"` and no note for `[mcp].worker_tools`, both tiers produce non-empty deferral notes where `wide_defer` is the wider of the two; the code returns `alpha`'s narrower note because `"alpha" < "zeta"`, while labeling it as applying to both lanes. The returned doctor note then understates the actual widest deferral.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:doctor_notes

chunk_findings.detail: This test creates a hard link named `worker-mcp-alias.json` to the current `worker-mcp-impl.json` and asserts that `alias` is not reported as “no longer in”. A hard link is a distinct directory entry with a distinct lane name, not the case-insensitive-filesystem collision the test claims to model. An unconfigured `alias` lane file is a real stale lane file and should be reported, just like `old` later in the same test. If `write_lanes` honors this assertion, it suppresses valid stale-lane warnings for any extra hard-linked lane name; conversely, the test still would not catch the original case-only macOS/Windows issue.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_a_lane_file_that_is_another_name_for_a_current_one_is_not_reported_stale

chunk_findings.detail: The test saves the exit code as `_code` but never asserts `_code != 0`. An implementation (or CLI wrapper) that catches the bad `lane_tools` value, prints `impl=bogus` without a traceback, and still exits 0 and proceeds with `adopt` would satisfy the assertion, contradicting the test’s stated “stops adopt” purpose.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_a_hand_edited_bad_lane_list_stops_adopt_with_the_reason_not_a_traceback

chunk_findings.detail: `wide` is sorted by lane name (`sorted(lane for lane, tier in lanes.items() if deferral_note(env, tier=tier))`), but the note text is then taken from `lanes[wide[0]]`, the alphabetically first lane. The docstring says the lane note should be “one note for the widest.” With a spec such as `[mcp].lane_tools = "beta=core\nalpha=auto"` where `auto` is the wider tier and its `deferral_note` text differs, this returns the `core` note for `alpha` and appends both lane names to that narrower note. The selection should order by tier width, not lane name.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:doctor_notes

chunk_findings.detail: The new final case asserts only that the single note contains "`all` tool tier" for `_cfg(worker="all", lanes="rev=all")`. A `doctor_notes` implementation that, when `worker_tools == "all"`, emits one generic all-tier note and then ignores the per-lane override would satisfy this assertion even though the lane `rev` is never reported—the exact regression this test is meant to prevent. The preceding lane-only case does require `"rev"` in the note, showing that the overlap case should likewise assert that the affected lane is named.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_the_doctor_counts_a_lane_on_the_whole_tool_list

chunk_findings.detail: The new stale-file check uses `lane.casefold() not in named`, which treats lane names as case-insensitive regardless of the filesystem. On a case-sensitive filesystem (Linux default), a leftover `worker-mcp-IMPL.json` is a distinct file from the configured `worker-mcp-impl.json`, but `IMPL.casefold()` equals `"impl"`, so it is skipped and never reported as “no longer in [mcp].lane_tools”. Concrete input: repo contains `.ddflow/local/worker-mcp-IMPL.json` and `[mcp].lane_tools = "impl=all"`; `write_lanes` writes `worker-mcp-impl.json`, sees the uppercase file, and suppresses the stale-lane warning even though that uppercase file remains orphaned. The previous `samefile` check handled this correctly; the replacement should consult the real filesystem case rules, for example `os.path.normcase`/`samefile`, not unconditional `casefold`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:write_lanes
